title: Why Taps Drip: Worn Washers and Valve Seats
description: An educational guide explaining the mechanical cause behind spout leaks in compression taps and how to address them correctly.
image_prompt: A detailed educational macro cross-section cutaway illustration of a brass compression tap stem assembly, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The image cleanly reveals the internal mechanism of a dual-handle brass faucet body. Inside the valve chamber, a threaded stem holds a black rubber washer at its base against a circular brass valve seat. The rubber washer displays realistic wear with micro-cracks and flattened edges along the sealing surface. Tiny water droplets are shown leaking past the compromised seal down through the spout outlet channel. Neutral studio lighting, clean gray-toned background, ultra-sharp focus on the internal brass geometry and washer interface. No text, no visual labels, no logos, no watermarks, no impossible plumbing connections.
visual_story: The visual focuses on the interior seal of a compression tap valve. The viewer can clearly see the relationship between the threaded brass stem, the black rubber washer, and the valve seat. By highlighting the flattened and cracked edge of the washer where it meets the metal seat, the visual demonstrates why water under pressure bypasses the seal and flows down into the spout.

on_image_text.explanation: Spout drips occur when the washer degrades or the brass valve seat becomes pitted.
on_image_text.takeaway: Replace the washer and inspect the seat—don't just force the handle tighter.
